metadata.title: Thermo-mechanical restraining frame experiment (COST TU1404 Task 3 - Turner et al.)
metadata.validation_method: Temperature and average restrained stress vs time, compared to Fig.10 and Fig.22-25. Core temperature and stress history.
metadata.validation_target: Fig.10: core temperature peak ~41 C at ~60 h, drop to ~21.5 C at formwork removal (265 h); average stress minimum -1.1 MPa at ~50 h, zero crossing ~100 h, +1.8 MPa just before stripping, jumping to +2.15 MPa and holding to 400 h. Core and corner are nearly identical because of the insulation.
metadata.notes: Updated with user-extracted figure data: core/corner temperature (data 17) and stress (data 18) from Fig.10/Fig.22/Fig.25. Files converted to time_h,T_degC and time_h,stress_MPa format matching x_col/y_col. RISKY remains for creep and insulation discrete modeling. CORRECTED 2026-08-22: (1) physical groups made disjoint -- overlapping tags on the end edges were dropped by meshio and crashed the run; (2) h corrected from 10/20 to 0.94/37.5 (insulation + longitudinal-slice perimeter, see boundary_conditions); (3) B3 q1-q4 recomputed from the mix; (4) thermal_aging added so the creep chain ages on equivalent time; (5) uy released along fixed_end, pinned at one node; (6) t_end extended to 400 h. Previous validation_target values (44 C @ 35 h, +1.1 MPa) misread Fig.10.
metadata._comment: Task 3 of COST benchmark, based on Turner et al. [9] restraining frame

entities._comment: PAPER_VALUE: specimen 3.7 x 0.25 x 0.25 m (Sec 2.3, Fig.8). 2D model length 3.7, height 0.25, thickness out-of-plane 0.25 modeled via plane_stress thickness.

physical_groups.name: surface_exposed
physical_groups._comment: BOTTOM + TOP edges ONLY. The two END edges convect through their own groups (fixed_end / spring_end) because a gmsh entity carrying two physical tags loses one when meshio reads the mesh: meshio keeps a single tag per entity, so with surface_exposed (tag 2) also covering the end edges, tags 3 and 4 never reached the mesh and resolve_location_to_nodes('fixed_end') raised. Physical groups on edges must be DISJOINT; several BCs may then name the same group.

physical_groups.name: spring_end
physical_groups._comment: Right end with spring support kF=1053 MN/m Fig.20

physical_groups.name: symmetry_dummy
physical_groups._comment: Dim-0 group auto-creates node at centre for point probe - ensures exact node at 1.85,0.125

physical_groups.name: pin_node
physical_groups._comment: Single node at (0,0) carrying uy=0. Fixing uy along the WHOLE fixed_end edge blocks the end's Poisson/thermal contraction in y and injects spurious local stress; one node is enough to remove the rigid-body mode.

physical_groups.name: corner_probe_node
physical_groups._comment: Forces a mesh node at the corner probe; without it the probe resolved 1.89e-2 m away from the nearest node.

mesh._comment: INFERRED: 50mm gives 74 elements along length, 5 through height, sufficient for thermal. Mechanical needs >=10 through bending depth? Bending not dominant, axial restraint dominant.

thermal_aging._comment: Canonical key -- the (temperature, displacement) pair is ambiguous between thermal_strain and thermal_aging, so it must be named exactly (D14).

temperature._comment_k: PAPER_VALUE: Table 8 thermal conductivity 2.4 W/(K m3) meaning W/mK
temperature._comment_rho: INFERRED: mix Table7: 300+145+2000+3=2448 kg/m3 minus water loss, approx 2333 used to match volumetric 2500 kJ/K/m3

degree_of_hydration._comment_Ea: PAPER_VALUE: Table8 activation energy 46,000 J/mol measured
degree_of_hydration._comment_sanity: dT_ad=Hu*c*alpha/(rho cp)=420e3*300*0.85/2.5e6=42.84K, initial 22C => 64.8C adiabatic, measured peak 44C, so BCs carry ~20K - passes

displacement._comment_E: IGNORED on the oofem backend -- the mps creep chain supplies the elastic response through b3_creep.q1. Kept for the legacy fem/ backend and for documentation. PAPER_VALUE Table 9: Ecm(28d) = 34.133 GPa.
displacement._comment_plane_stress: INFERRED: specimen is beam-like 3.7m long 0.25x0.25 cross-section, loaded axially, plane stress with thickness 0.25m gives correct axial stiffness EA

autogenous_shrinkage._comment_shrinkage_max: PAPER_VALUE: final shrinkage 0.05 per mille =0.05/1000=5e-5, compressive negative -5e-5 Sec 2.3
autogenous_shrinkage._comment_age: PAPER_VALUE: setting time 10.5h=0.4375d Table8, material age at t=0 for shrinkage-only runs
autogenous_shrinkage._comment_model: On OOFEM this is B4 asymptote on equivalent age, not alpha/alpha_inf, divergence D9 noted

b3_creep._comment_q:
Bazant & Baweja B3, computed from Table 7 + Table 9: c = 300 kg/m3, w/c = 145/300 = 0.4833, a/c = 2000/300 = 6.667, fcm28 = 57.8 MPa, E28 = 34133 MPa.
  q1 = 0.6/E28                  = 1.758e-11 1/Pa
  q2 = 185.4*c^0.5*fcm^-0.9     = 8.336e-11 1/Pa
  q3 = 0.29*(w/c)^4*q2          = 1.319e-12 1/Pa
  q4 = 20.3*(a/c)^-0.7          = 5.380e-12 1/Pa
Matches Table 16: Team 2 'estimated the B3 parameters q1-q4 from the composition of concrete mixture and compressive strength (fc, w/c, a/c)'. Previous q1=1.5e-11 and q3=2e-12 were hand estimates.
b3_creep._comment_E28: PAPER_VALUE Table 9: Ecm(28d) = 34,133 MPa. Used only to derive q1 -- materials.concrete.displacement.E is IGNORED by the mps chain (mps/host.py: 'E is deliberately ABSENT: the elastic response of an mps material comes from the chain (q1), not E'). Aging stiffness comes from mps solidification, which is the paper's Fig.24-right behaviour.

thermal_aging._comment: Without this section coupledanalysistype stays 0 (Basic) and the mps creep chain ages on REAL time while the specimen sits at 35-41 C for days. Every team used a maturity clock (Sec. 3.2: 'all of them were related to heat release, expressed with the equivalent age of concrete, teq').
thermal_aging._comment_kTm: INFERRED: kTm replaces ln(h) in the microprestress equation. Table 16 gives Team 2 'sealed conditions'; self-desiccation h = 0.98 -> kTm = -ln(0.98) = 0.0202. Same convention as OOFEM regression test MPS_05_in.sm.
thermal_aging._comment_mus: INFERRED: OOFEM muS = c0*c1^(p-1)*q4*(p-1)^p with p=2 -> muS = c0*c1*q4 = 0.235 1/(MPa*day) * 1 MPa * 5.380e-6 1/MPa = 1.264e-6 1/(MPa*day) = 1.4633e-17 1/(Pa*s). c0 is Havlasek & Jirasek's calibrated value, c1 = 1 MPa assumed (k1 and c0 are only identifiable as a product).
thermal_aging._comment_Q_E_over_R: PAPER_VALUE Table 8: measured Ea = 46,000 J/mol -> Ea/R = 46000/8.314 = 5532.8 K. Set explicitly so the creep maturity clock agrees with hydratingConcreteMat's; oofem's default is 2700 K (Bazant 1995) and mps does NOT read the hydration degree (D14).

initial_conditions._comment: PAPER_VALUE: ambient 22C Sec 2.3, concrete initial assumed same

boundary_conditions._comment_alpha:
CORRECTED. Two compounding errors were fixed here.
(a) The 10 / 20 W/(m2K) of Sec. 2.3 are NOT concrete-surface values: Fig.8 shows the specimen wrapped in 27 mm formwork PLUS 160 mm XPS (Table 6), and Sec. 4.3.2 states the lumped equivalent 'was computed to be h = 0.5 W/(m2K)'. Independent check: the measured cooling in Fig.10 has tau ~ 89 h; h=0.5 on the true 0.25x0.25 section gives tau = 87 h, while h=10 gives 4.3 h.
(b) This model is a LONGITUDINAL 3.7 x 0.25 slice, whose cooled perimeter/area is 2*(3.7+0.25)/0.925 = 8.54 1/m against the real cross-section's 1.0/0.0625 = 16 1/m -- it sheds heat at half the correct rate per unit volume, so h must be scaled by 16/8.54 = 1.874.
=> h = 0.5*1.874 = 0.94 while insulated, 20*1.874 = 37.5 after stripping.
Verified: with the raw 10/20 the run peaks at 32.4 C @ 15.2 h (measured 41 C @ ~60 h) and is back at ambient by 100 h; an FD check of this geometry with 0.94 gives 45.7 C @ 36.6 h, matching the paper's own lumped-BC result in Fig.23 (47.5 C @ 42 h). RISKY: the paper is explicit that reproducing the EXPERIMENT (41 C @ 60 h) needs discrete formwork+XPS elements -- heat stored in the insulation both lowers and delays the peak. This value reproduces the teams' simplified boundary condition, not the measurement.
boundary_conditions._comment_alpha_paper: PAPER_VALUE Sec.2.3: h = 10 W/(m2K) in formwork, 20 free, formwork removed at 265 h = 954000 s.

boundary_conditions._comment_alpha: Same convection as the rest of the surface; a separate entry only because gmsh entities carry one physical tag (see surface_exposed).
boundary_conditions._comment_alpha_paper: PAPER_VALUE Sec.2.3: h = 10 W/(m2K) in formwork, 20 free, formwork removed at 265 h = 954000 s.

boundary_conditions._comment_alpha: Same convection as the rest of the surface; a separate entry only because gmsh entities carry one physical tag (see surface_exposed).
boundary_conditions._comment_alpha_paper: PAPER_VALUE Sec.2.3: h = 10 W/(m2K) in formwork, 20 free, formwork removed at 265 h = 954000 s.

boundary_conditions._comment: Single node -- removes the rigid-body vertical mode without over-constraining the end.

boundary_conditions._comment_alpha: INFERRED: kF=1053 MN/m=1.053e9 N/m total, area Ac=0.25*0.25=0.0625 m2, alpha=kF/Ac=1.6848e10 N/m3. PAPER_VALUE kF Fig.20, INFERRED alpha conversion.

time_stepping._comment_t_end: 400 h. All three reference curves run to 400 h and the post-stripping plateau (265-400 h) carries the benchmark's headline result -- the previous 300 h cut it off.
